Unit 19 - Relevance & Redundancy — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 19 - relevance & redundancy questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Arrange sentences for flow.
  • Use accurate transitions.
  • Keep relevant, clear wording.

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Sentence — The data were inconclusive( ) more experiments are necessary.

Question 1. Which choice completes the sentence correctly?

  • , and
  • , which
  • ;
  • :
Independent clauses need a semicolon or coordinating conjunction; best is C.

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Sentence — Neither the analysts nor the manager were available.

Question 2. Which choice corrects the error?

  • was
  • were being
  • are
  • have been

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Sentence — The committee finished the report—their review complete— they submitted it.

Question 3. Which punctuation best improves clarity?

  • comma after ‘complete’ only
  • dash after ‘complete’ only
  • dashes around ‘their review complete’
  • no punctuation

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Sentence — Walking to the bus, the rain soaked my jacket.

Question 4. Which revision corrects the dangling modifier?

  • While walking to the bus, my jacket was soaked.
  • While I was walking to the bus, rain soaked my jacket.
  • While walking, rain was soaking.
  • Walking to the bus soaking rain.

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Sentence — She studied; consequently, she improved her score.

Question 5. Which transition best shows cause and effect?

  • however
  • consequently
  • similarly
  • instead
